title: Python: ALIAS, a local with one binding to Cls.attr or mod.attr resolves as that attribute does (DEC-303 (a23) item 2)
description: DEC-303 (a23) item 2, verbatim: 'ALIAS is admitted. A local with exactly one binding, to Cls.attr or mod.attr, where that attribute resolves under the rules in force (A2, module attribute, Class.method), resolves as that attribute does. This is item 2 of (a22) (every binding enumerable from the scope's text, with the nonlocal proviso) composed with A2. Any second binding, or a right-hand side that does not itself resolve, stays unresolved.' Third in the (a23) build order after M1 and R4 (ALIAS, TS, Q1, (a25), NB-b, step 5) that releases the (a36) hold on the fresh blind sample. The call form is a bare call of the local (f = mod.func; f(), g = Cls.method; g(obj)). Lessons from K1, LIT, M1 and R4 to apply BEFORE the first push: enumerate every way the local gets a second binding with enumerableBindings (never S3 localNames), including a nonlocal write from a nested scope (read in the scope holding it: RawBinding.origin) and a comprehension target (not a nonlocal binding, RawBinding.comprehension); enumerate every way the RIGHT-HAND SIDE's own names get a second binding in EVERY module the resolution reads (the importing module, the defining module, a re-export hop: Cls, mod and the attribute), each with its own refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site and the receiver or name bin is unchanged; refuse module-level stars; read stars, globals, class bodies and annotations; every refusal fixture asserts the edge half (symbol ids) and the bin half. Report the five-pin per-site corpus diff, with every in-repo edge named, to the leader before the clear. Open follow-ups that touch this rule: GCLI-112 (PEP 695 type parameters bind no name).

acceptanceCriteria.text: a local with exactly ONE binding, a plain unannotated assignment whose right-hand side is Cls.attr or mod.attr (a dotted name of one segment after a name), where that right-hand side resolves under the rules in force (A2 module.Class.method, a module attribute, Class.method), resolves a bare call of the local as that attribute does, with red-before fixtures and positive and negative twins

each of these leaves the call unresolved, each with its own refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site (by symbol id) and the call stays in its current bin (bin delta against the same source with the call replaced): a second binding of the local by any form (rebind, augmented, for, with-as, except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, import, def, class, tuple or star target, annotation, type alias, global declaration, a nonlocal write from a nested scope of any depth); an annotated binding; a right-hand side that does not itself resolve (a call, a literal, an unresolved or external attribute, a deeper chain, a name); a right-hand side whose Cls, mod or attribute name has a second binding in the importing module or in the module defining it (rebind, for, with-as, walrus, def, global write, star), or behind a re-export hop; a module-level star import; a class-body binding of the local

each rule has a mutation check that goes red (mutants listed by name, equivalent mutants said so), and a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with every in-repo edge it creates or removes named per site and sent to the leader before the clear
